findings.claim: The read-back requires the title and body to 'equal' the submitted files, with no normalization rule. GitHub can alter line endings and trailing whitespace, so a successful write could read back as a mismatch and be reported `unknown`. `unknown` stops every later write and retry, so the run halts even though the write succeeded. The comparison needs a defined normalization, or it will give false `unknown` results.

Step 2 says 'Read each candidate' but does not carry the SKILL.md bound (only title-matching candidates, at most 10, stop if more). A reader of the procedure alone could read up to 1000 search results. The two files split one rule and the procedure's wording is unbounded.

Step 5 does not say what happens when the printed URL is missing or unparsable, so NUMBER or COMMENT_ID cannot be derived. The read-back cannot run in that case. Only the 'read-back that fails' sentence at line 18 might cover it, and it does not say so explicitly.

evidence: Reviewed the full diff of all five changed paths for the recall and readability lenses.
The read-back comparison is defined as exact equality (procedure.md line 18). The diff says nothing about normalizing text that GitHub may alter.
SKILL.md bounds duplicate reads to 10 title-matching candidates, while procedure.md step 2 says 'each candidate' and step 1 uses --limit 1000.
